title: Sell Mineral Rights in Alba, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Alba, PA | Bradford County
metaDescription: Alba, PA mineral owners in Bradford County's dry-gas core: get a clear cash offer on your Marcellus royalty, no obligation.
heroLead: Alba sits in Bradford County, the dry-gas heart of the northeastern Marcellus play, where some of the earliest and biggest leasing deals in the whole state got signed.
intro: Bradford County was ground zero for the northeastern Marcellus rush, and Alba-area families were part of that first wave of leasing back in the mid-to-late 2000s, when companies like Chesapeake Energy locked up huge blocks of acreage across the county almost overnight. If your family signed one of those early leases, you've likely been collecting a royalty for close to two decades now, through a lot of ups and downs in gas prices and well performance.
We know what it's like to hold a mineral interest that long and still not fully understand every line on the statement. That's exactly the conversation we want to have with you.

sections.heading: Dry gas, not wet gas, and why that matters
paragraphs: Unlike the wet-gas counties in southwestern Pennsylvania, Bradford County's Marcellus production is largely dry gas, meaning there's little to no natural gas liquids content requiring separate processing. That generally means a simpler, if still present, post-production deduction structure on your royalty statement, mostly gathering and compression rather than liquids fractionation.
This is also some of the thickest, most productive dry-gas Marcellus rock in the entire play, which is part of why operators moved so aggressively to lease this county early on.

sections.heading: An early lease means an older well
paragraphs: If your family's Alba-area lease dates to the early leasing rush, the well on your unit is likely well past its steepest decline period by now, settled into a slower, more predictable production tail. That production history is useful; it means we're valuing your interest against real, years-long performance data rather than a projection.

sections.heading: Confirming what an early-era lease actually says
paragraphs: Leases signed during the initial rush sometimes carry different royalty and deduction terms than what became standard later, once owners and their attorneys had more experience negotiating. We review your specific lease language, traced through the Bradford County Recorder of Deeds, before quoting a number.

faqs.question: Why does my Bradford County deduction line look smaller than what I hear about from southwestern PA?
faqs.answer: Dry gas requires less processing than wet gas, so post-production deductions here are typically lower relative to gross value, though they still apply under current Pennsylvania law.

faqs.question: My lease is from 2008. Is that too old to be relevant?
faqs.answer: Not at all. Many of the earliest Bradford County leases are still active and held by production. We'll review your specific lease terms regardless of its age.

faqs.question: How predictable is a well this far into its production life?
faqs.answer: Generally more predictable than a new well, since years of actual production data give us a real decline curve to work from rather than an estimate.
